Gen.G Esports (often abbreviated as Gen.G and officially short for Generation Gaming, and formerly known as KSV eSports) is an American esports organization.

Timeline

[edit]
  • 2019
  • 2020
  • 2021
  • 2024
  • Show All
  • December 6th - Gen.G Esports enter Counter-Strike: Global Offensive with the acquisition of Cloud9's core, consisting of autimatic, daps, and koosta. Additionally, Cloud9's assistant coach, Elmapuddy, joins as the team's coach. [1]
  • December 9th - Gen.G Esports acquire s0m from Team Envy. [2]
  • December 22nd - Gen.G Esports acquire BnTeT from TYLOO. [3]
  • September 11th - daps steps down from the active lineup. [4]
  • September 17th - daps's contract expires and he leaves the team. [5]
  • October 7th - s0m retires from Counter-Strike: Global Offensive after being acquired by NRG Esports' VALORANT division. [6]
  • January 21st - koosta retires from competitive Counter-Strike: Global Offensive after being transferred to Gen.G Esports's VALORANT roster. [7]
  • January 24th - BnTeT is acquired by EXTREMUM and Elmapuddy is acquired by Cloud9. [8][9]
  • February 4th - autimatic retires from competitive Counter-Strike: Global Offensive after being acquired by T1's VALORANT division. [10]
  • February 21st - Gen.G Esports announce their return to Counter-Strike with the signing of a roster consisting of: s1, rosar, heartZ, ScreaMy, miracle, and coach KYO. [11]
  • April 30th - Gen.G Esports part ways with Siyi and rosar. [12]
  • May 20th - Gen.G Esports sign Erye and Resay. [12]
  • October 21st - Gen.G Esports disbands. [13]
